ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Evel Knievel Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient: chronic pain from old fractures, diabetes, and raised liver tests with low platelets on today's tests: hepatitis C and liver work-up, NSAIDs stopped, alcohol counseling, and hepatology review booked. Concerns: Pain in the back, hips and knees every day from old fractures, worse in the morning and after travel; ibuprofen three times a day for years; Tired for months; noticed small red spots on his chest and wonders whether the old transfusions or his drinking have hurt his liver; He wants to keep walking and playing golf and does not want to depend on strong pain pills; Two falls in the past year; he worries about breaking another bone. [S]

tr.td: Ultrasound of the abdomen with Doppler: nodular liver surface and coarse echotexture; no focal liver lesion; spleen 14.2 cm; portal vein patent with forward flow; no ascites; gallbladder normal
Transient elastography (FibroScan) at the hepatology visit: median liver stiffness 26.8 kPa (interquartile range under 30% of the median), controlled attenuation parameter 248 dB/m

Outpatient physical therapy assessment: limited hip and knee range from old fractures, slow gait, Timed Up and Go 13 seconds, poor single-leg balance; aquatic therapy twice a week and a home exercise program; cane for long distances

Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry: femoral neck T-score -2.6, total hip -2.2, lumbar spine -1.9 (read with caution because of old fractures and degenerative change); 10-year FRAX risk of major osteoporotic fracture 14% and hip fracture 4.1%
Surveillance ultrasound of the liver six months after the baseline scan: nodular liver, no focal lesion; spleen 13.8 cm; no ascites (LI-RADS US-1, negative)

tr.td: New patient: chronic pain from old fractures, diabetes, and raised liver tests with low platelets on today's tests: hepatitis C and liver work-up, NSAIDs stopped, alcohol counseling, and hepatology review booked
Hepatitis C confirmed with compensated cirrhosis: elastography, hepatology consultation, carvedilol for portal hypertension, statin, vaccines, and the antiviral plan
Day 1 of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir: drug interaction check, carvedilol titration, glucose monitoring, vitamin D, and the bone density plan
End of 12 weeks of antiviral treatment: liver tests, glucose monitoring in cirrhosis, osteoporosis, pain, and abstinence
Cure confirmed (SVR12): six-month liver cancer surveillance, cirrhosis care after cure, and transplant criteria reviewed

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Hepatology consultation within three weeks to confirm and stage chronic liver disease and plan antiviral treatment if hepatitis C is confirmed

Liver work-up for raised transaminases and low platelets: hepatitis C antibody with reflex RNA, hepatitis B surface antigen, core antibody and surface antibody, hepatitis A IgG, HIV, INR, ultrasound of the abdomen, and FIB-4 from today's tests

Pain care safe in liver disease: stop ibuprofen and omeprazole; acetaminophen up to 2 g a day; topical diclofenac for the knees; no opioids; physical and aquatic therapy; heat, pacing and sleep routines; pain coping skills
Alcohol: brief counseling toward stopping completely, because alcohol speeds liver scarring; follow-up AUDIT-C at each visit; counseling or medicine for alcohol use offered if he cannot stop

Sofosbuvir-velpatasvir one tablet daily for 12 weeks under the AASLD-IDSA simplified pathway for compensated cirrhosis, after hepatitis B testing and a drug interaction check (no proton pump inhibitor; watch for muscle pain on atorvastatin); glucose monitoring for hypoglycemia; HCV RNA and liver tests 12 or more weeks after the last dose

Carvedilol for clinically significant portal hypertension (liver stiffness 25 kPa or more), started at 6.25 mg and raised to 12.5 mg daily if blood pressure allows; no screening endoscopy while he takes it; liver stiffness and platelets rechecked a year after cure
Liver cancer surveillance by ultrasound with alpha-fetoprotein every six months, continuing after cure because cirrhosis remains
Vaccines for chronic liver disease: hepatitis A (two doses) and hepatitis B (two doses), then influenza, pneumococcal and zoster vaccines at the preventive visit

Teaching on decompensation (swelling of the abdomen or legs, black stools or vomiting blood, confusion, yellow eyes) with same-day contact; transplant referral only if decompensation occurs or the MELD-Na reaches 15

Diabetes care adapted to cirrhosis: metformin continued while kidney function is normal and he does not drink; continuous glucose monitoring because the A1c can read falsely low; moderate-intensity statin; yearly eye and foot examinations and urine albumin
Falls and fractures: physical therapy and a home safety review; vitamin D; bone density scan, since cirrhosis, alcohol and many old fractures raise the risk of osteoporosis

Zoledronic acid 5 mg intravenously once a year, after vitamin D repletion and a normal calcium, rather than an oral bisphosphonate because of portal hypertension; dental review first; bone density again in two years
Depression and distress screening at each visit, and plain explanations with written information
